analysis: The changed files in this batch are documentation only: docs/developer/build.md, whose patch excerpt shows a date bump and new text at head lines 492-501, and docs/developer/test.md, with a date bump and a test-description paragraph at base/head line ~2192. The supplied head_text for build.md starts at line 893, so the new lines 492-501 are visible only in the patch excerpt. The docs describe CI runner-label isolation: the route client sends X-Darkbloom-Run-Scoped-Labels: 1 and accepts only profile labels ending in -run-<github.run_id>. Generic or other-run labels fall back to Blacksmith without broadening the accepted labels. The described behavior tightens CI runner selection, so a runner from an older workflow run cannot pick up a job. No provider code, App Attest authorization (TB-011, T-053/T-054), cache storage (T-041) or coordinator wire contract (TB-002) changes. The documentation makes no new security claims about those assets, and the existing statements about lack of Apple/physical qualification are unchanged. The canonical threat model has no CI or runner trust boundary, so this CI hardening is outside the model, and I identify no regression or invalidated assumption. Remaining uncertainty: the actual route client and workflow implementation is not in this batch, so I could not verify that the code matches the documented label-matching behavior. The documentation changes do not alter security controls.
